title: Instance.Parent
summary: Where an instance lives in the hierarchy. Setting it moves/replicates the object; nil removes it from the world. Destroyed instances have Parent permanently locked to nil.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Current container. Writing moves the instance (and triggers replication when crossing the server→client boundary rules). Destroy() locks it at nil forever.

explanation.whatItIs: An object's address. Change the address, the object moves — into the world, into storage, or out of existence (nil).
explanation.whyItExists: The DataModel tree IS the game; parenting is how objects enter and leave it.
whenToUse: Spawning: build object, configure, parent LAST
Soft removal: Parent = nil keeps the object alive in memory for reuse
Moving objects between containers (e.g., tool Backpack → Character happens automatically)
whenNotToUse: Parenting before configuring — each property write can replicate; configure first
Parenting server-only content into replicated containers by accident
tips: Create→configure→parent pattern is both faster and replication-cleaner
Parent=nil is reversible; Destroy is not
Setting Parent to a destroyed instance errors ('The Parent property is locked')
commonMistakes: Parenting half-built objects into workspace (visible pop-in, extra replication)
Assuming Parent=nil destroyed the object — it's still in memory, still referenced
Client parenting expecting server effects — client-side parenting only affects that client

examples.title: Configure-first pattern
examples.code:
-- ❌ Replicates half-finished state:
-- local p = Instance.new("Part"); p.Parent = workspace; p.Size = ...; p.Color = ...

-- ✅ One clean arrival:
local p = Instance.new("Part")
p.Size = Vector3.new(4, 1, 4)
p.Anchored = true
p.Color = Color3.fromRGB(200, 50, 50)
p.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
p.Parent = workspace   -- last!

-- Soft-hide, keep alive:
p.Parent = nil
-- Later: p.Parent = workspace   (still configured!)
